Evidence base

Specific evidence, visible limitations.

SafeNet uses research to define the problem and shape safer design choices. A source does not prove that SafeNet has already achieved an outcome; prototype, pilot and impact evidence remain separate.

Zimbabwean campus cyberbullying

A case study surveyed 380 undergraduates at one Zimbabwean higher-education institution. Seventy-five per cent reported receiving a threatening message on campus. The finding is institution-specific and is not a national or women-only prevalence estimate.

Sibanda, “Cyberbullying in Higher and Tertiary Education institutions in Zimbabwe” ↗

Zimbabwean university e-safety intervention

This action-research study supports the value of explicit e-safety education, peer structures and clear reporting routes while illustrating why any outcome claim needs a defined population and method.

Read the peer-reviewed article ↗

Women’s experiences of cybersexual harassment

A qualitative Zimbabwean university study documents explicit-image abuse, demands for intimate material and sexually explicit hate speech reported by female students. It informs the need for women-centred language and support choices without being treated as a prevalence estimate.

Read the study ↗

SafeTech Africa HackLab call

The call centres safe digital spaces, youth leadership, privacy, low-bandwidth access, disability inclusion, measurable impact and community-owned approaches to technology-facilitated violence.
